$comment: Request/response JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12) for sandbox-runner.postman_collection.json, rendered into its items' descriptions and ENDPOINTS_SCHEMAS.md (linked from ENDPOINTS.md). Edit here, then: uv run --no-sync python scripts/api_schemas.py render. A schema whose $comment says `generated from …` is rewritten by unit-tests/sandbox/test_api_schemas.py (API_SCHEMAS_UPDATE=1): never edit one. The rest is hand-written from runner/app.py, operations.py, sandbox_mcp.py, tool_server.py, spawner.py and common.jobs; that test validates real responses against it (a fake Docker client and the job table in memory, no Docker, no Postgres). The MCP envelope follows the MCP SDK's models (open objects) as FastMCP 3.4.5 fills them.

sandbox_id.description: A sandbox's internal id: its job row's id, 12 hex characters

session_id.description: Persistent handle across turns (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`; a generated one is 12 URL-safe characters)

app_status.description: On a fresh spawn (or a warming / existing sandbox) a placeholder `{code: 200, latency_ms: 0, note}` -- the readiness gate already passed; after a write, one live HTTP probe of the runtime's readiness path (3 s deadline): `{code, latency_ms}` for a real HTTP reply, `{error}` for a network failure

example_files.description: A minimal `files` map for the runtime

runtime.description: The runtime the session was spawned under

startup_output.description: A tail of /tmp/sandbox.log -- after a write, only what the dev server printed since this write

recreated.description: True: the session's container was gone and was respawned (self-heal)

similarity.description: Line similarity of the new content to the existing file

detail_rewrite.description: The rewrite guard: a listed path already exists as a text file of 30+ lines (WRITE_GUARD_MIN_LINES) and keeps >= 50 % of its lines (WRITE_GUARD_SIMILARITY); no file of the call was written

content.description: The first `max_bytes_per_file` bytes; a truncated text file is cut on a character boundary

error.description: `not found`, or why the path could not be read (`size` 0, empty `content`)

file_entry_meta.description: A `file_entry` without `content` (the contents are in the tool's text)

session_row.description: One running sandbox, read back from its job row

last_used_at.description: Bumped by every write / read_file / edit_file / exec

sessions.description: Every running sandbox on the deployment, newest first -- no per-user filtering

entrypoint.description: The caller's entrypoint, else the runtime's default

sandbox_jobs.description: The newest 20 job rows (PostgresRegistry.list_all), terminal ones included

max_concurrent.description: The registry tracks no ceiling (the runner's semaphore does)

end_line.description: The last line shown (start_line - 1 for an empty window)

total_lines.description: Lines in the file (in its first READ_FILE_MAX_BYTES when `file_truncated`)

truncated.description: More lines follow `end_line` (ask again with offset = end_line + 1)

file_truncated.description: Only the first READ_FILE_MAX_BYTES were read

content.description: `cat -n` style: the line number, a TAB, the line

start_line.description: The (first) replaced region in the NEW file

match_lines.description: The first line of every replacement (up to 20)

startup_output.description: What the dev server printed after this edit

exit_code.description: -1 when the command timed out or the exec failed

truncated.description: Earlier output was dropped (the LAST EXEC_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES are kept)

lines_requested.description: The `lines` asked for (the tail is clamped to 1..1000)

logs.description: The tail of /tmp/sandbox.log: the app's stdout + stderr and `[browser]` lines; empty is not an error

cursor.description: An opaque token representing the current pagination position

job_base.$comment: generated from common.jobs.model.JobBase — do not edit
job_base.description:
Snapshot of one job at a point in time.

Fields:
    job_id: 12-char hex identifier assigned at registration.
    phase: Freeform string; each consumer defines its own convention.
        Interceptor-api uses ``"cloning" | "capturing" | "actions" |
        "cleaning_up"`` (``"actions"`` while a capture's
        ``page_script`` / ``actions`` run);
        classifier uses ``"staging" | "pending" | "processing" |
        "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled"``.
    created_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the job was registered.
    updated_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last phase / result / error
        transition. Equals ``created_at`` for a job that hasn't transitioned.
    elapsed_seconds: Wall-clock seconds since ``created_at``, computed at
        snapshot time from a monotonic clock. Present for ephemeral jobs;
        derived from ``created_at`` for persistent (SQLite-backed) jobs
        where the monotonic anchor is process-local and doesn't survive
        restarts.
    metadata: Consumer-defined dict describing the job. Typically the
        result of a pydantic ``BaseModel.model_dump()``.
    result: Populated on successful completion for persistent backends.
        Ephemeral backends never set this — a completed ephemeral job is
        already gone from the registry.
    error: Populated on failure for persistent backends. Same caveat as
        ``result`` for ephemeral.
job_base.title: JobBase

POST /v1/sandbox/run.description: A field validator's refusal (a file over SANDBOX_MAX_FILE_BYTES, a payload over SANDBOX_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, a reserved `env` key, a malformed `session_id` / `chat_id`, a negative `ttl_seconds`) is FastAPI's 422; 429 the pool is full; 500 a Docker spawn error.

schema.$comment: generated from models.RunRequest — do not edit

runtime.description: One of the keys in runtimes.RUNTIMES
runtime.title: Runtime

files.description: Path → content map. On the first call for a session this is the initial file set. On a follow-up call (same session_id) it is an overlay — paths given here overwrite files in the running container, unlisted files are left alone. Values are either raw UTF-8 strings, or {"encoding": "base64", "content": "..."} for binary payloads (images, PDFs, wheels). Per-file cap: SANDBOX_MAX_FILE_BYTES; total cap: SANDBOX_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES.
files.title: Files

entrypoint.description: Shell command inside the sandbox; must bind to port 80
entrypoint.title: Entrypoint

ttl_seconds.description: Idle TTL in seconds. Omit, null or 0 for SANDBOX_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS; a negative value is refused. Server clamps to SANDBOX_HARD_TTL_SECONDS.
ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds

session_id.description: Persistent identifier for a preview across turns. Omit on the first call; the server generates one and returns it. Pass the same value back on follow-up calls to update files in place — no respawn, same URL, dev server hot-reloads.
session_id.title: Session Id

deletes.description: Relative paths (under /app) to delete on a follow-up call. Ignored on the first call. Absolute paths and '..' are rejected.
deletes.title: Deletes

env.description: Process env vars set inside the container. Immutable after spawn (respawned self-heal replays the same env). Reserved keys HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/PYTHONUNBUFFERED/TERM/etc. are rejected — those are runner-controlled invariants.
env.title: Env

recreate_if_gone.description: If the session's container is gone, respawn a fresh one under the same session_id (env preserved; in-container files and exec-installed packages LOST). Default true — run is the one-shot path. Set false to get a 409 instead.
recreate_if_gone.title: Recreate If Gone

overwrite.description: Follow-up calls only: allow replacing an existing text file of 30+ lines with content that keeps most of its lines. Without it such a write is refused with 409 rewrite_of_existing_file — use edit_file for changes to part of a file. New files, small files, binary files and genuine rewrites are never refused.
overwrite.title: Overwrite

chat_id.description: Id of the chat/conversation this call belongs to. When set and no session_id is given, the runner reuses the chat's existing live sandbox instead of spawning a second one — so one conversation maps to one container. Pass it on every call for a chat and you never have to thread session_id yourself.
chat_id.title: Chat Id

MCP run.description: The JSON-RPC response's `result.structuredContent` (one SSE `data:` message); `result.content[0].text` is the prose the model reads. The text ends with the fenced ```html block the model must relay verbatim. `recreate_if_gone` is always true.

arguments.$comment: generated from app._mcp:run — do not edit

runtime.description: Runtime for the sandbox. One of the names in get_runtime_types.

files.description: Path → content map. First call (no session_id): full initial file set. Follow-up (with session_id): overlay — only NEW files; change existing ones with edit_file. Values are UTF-8 str or {encoding:'base64', content:'...'} for binaries.

entrypoint.description: Shell command inside the sandbox, must bind port 80. Leave unset for the runtime's default. Rejected for runtimes with allows_custom_entrypoint=false. Ignored on follow-up calls.

ttl_seconds.description: Idle TTL in seconds. Omit, null or 0 for the default (SANDBOX_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS); a negative value is refused. Server clamps to SANDBOX_HARD_TTL_SECONDS.

session_id.description: Handle for a persistent preview. OMIT on the first call, PASS on follow-ups to update in place.

deletes.description: Relative paths under /app to remove on a follow-up call.

env.description: Process env vars. Applied only on the first call. Reserved keys (HTTP_PROXY, PYTHONUNBUFFERED, etc.) rejected.

chat_id.description: Id of the chat you're answering in. With no session_id, the runner reuses this chat's existing container instead of spawning a new one — so repeated run calls in one chat update the same preview even if you lost the session_id. Pass it on every run for the chat.

overwrite.description: Follow-up calls only. Set true ONLY to deliberately replace an existing text file of 30+ lines with content that keeps 50% or more of its lines. Without it that write is refused (rewrite_of_existing_file) — use edit_file for such changes.

result.description: The session and its preview, or an error

iframe_html.description: The preview page the fenced block carries

oneOf.description: An HTTP error with a structured `detail`, returned as a normal tool result

status.description: The HTTP status the operation raised
